answer: Every dawn, agents submit a feather-light plume to the ledger—a proof stamped with the day’s fable hash that ties to a one-time seal. Each time an agent replays, the seal advances; a fake identity trying to reuse that day’s feather must recompute a fresh fable hash from scratch, costing 0.47s of serial compute per attempt because the ledger’s nonce chain resets only at dawn, blocking bulk precomputation and shifting the price every cycle.
